title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
event_hint: DAC 2026 paper proposing sparse matrix inference acceleration for LLMs on GPUs
problem: At moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%), existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) cannot outperform dense counterparts, limiting inference acceleration while maintaining model quality.
mechanism: Three-layer matrix storage format: (i) Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance (PDD) encoding for matrix compression with low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) lightweight Residual Layer (CSR format) for remaining non-zeros. Co-optimized SpMM kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores with pipelined execution overlapping computation with memory access.

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer at 50% sparsity
Kernel achieves up to 1.81× speedup over FlashLLM at 50% sparsity
End-to-end inference throughput up to 41.4% higher than FlashLLM for OPT-30B
Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline
Format conversion cost is one-time: 41.1s for OPT-30B, 92.6s for OPT-66B

evaluation_context: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs with 80GB HBM3, NVLink interconnect; OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm; batch sizes 8/16/32; sparsity levels 50%/60%/70%; input/output sequence length 512; GCC 12.3.0 and NVCC 12.6.
limitations: Does not outperform FlashLLM under high sparsity due to zero-padding requirements; constrained during compute-bound prefill phase with large N (runs slower than cuBLAS); targets decoding phase optimization; requires GPUs with sparse tensor cores and HBM; incurs slightly higher memory usage than SpInfer due to bitmap encoding in baseline method. Absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds not reported. HBM bandwidth utilization or memory traffic measurements not provided. Power consumption or performance-per-watt not measured. Supplement contains only acknowledgments and references—no additional experimental data addressing evidence gaps.
project_relevance: Addresses GPU memory bandwidth bottleneck in LLM inference through sparse matrix computation co-design with modern GPU hardware (sparse tensor cores + HBM). Relevant to direction on AI accelerator memory interface and hardware-software co-design. Demonstrates 1.64× kernel speedup and 21.4% memory reduction at 50% sparsity on H100, showing how algorithm-hardware specialization can extract performance from memory-bound workloads. However, absolute throughput numbers (tokens/second), HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, and power efficiency metrics are not reported—key evidence gaps for assessing real-world deployment value.

evidence_gaps.question: What is the absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds for OPT-30B and OPT-66B at batch sizes 8/16/32?
